summary: Benoît Vermander is a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Sciences Po, Yale, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director at the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and became a professor at Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Faure works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology, having studied under Paul Demiéville and Seizan Yanagida and earned doctorates in Paris. He held academic posts at Cornell (~1983–1987), Stanford (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

Bernard Frank was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as director at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1979–1983) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernard Goldman was a scholar of archaeology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1950–1958) and held a post at Wayne State University from circa 1954 to 1986.

Bernard Williams was a philosopher who studied at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1951). He held academic posts at University College London (~1959–1964) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian and archaeologist. He held academic posts at the University of Oldenburg from circa 1987 to 1993 and at the University of Heidelberg around 2003.

Bernfried Schlerath was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied under Paul Thieme (~1948–1956). He held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1956–1964), the University of Marburg (~1964–1967), and Free University of Berlin (~1974–1992).
Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist who succeeded Heinrich Lüders. He held an academic post at the University of Berlin from circa 1937 to 1945.

Bernhard Forssman is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1955–1960). He held posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nürnberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Leopold von Schroeder and Franz Kielhorn across several universities. He held positions at the University of Vienna (~1909–1938), the Tibetan-Iranian Institute / Asia Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp and attended Zurich, Berlin, Göttingen, and Paris. He held several teaching posts at the University of Zurich in 1833, 1835–1837, and 1845.

Bernhard Karlgren was a sinologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915). He subsequently held posts at Uppsala University (~1913–1918) and the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist educated at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne. His career included posts at the Nepal Research Centre (~1970–1972), the University of Cologne (1966–1976), Kiel University (1974–1993), and the University of Leipzig (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman was a Buddhist studies practitioner educated at the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn, NYU, and UCLA, who studied under Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers (1980).

Berthe Jansen is a tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford under Jonathan A. Silk. She was a research fellow at Heidelberg University (~2015) and Numata visiting professor at Leiden (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, Heymann Steinthal, and Rudolf Haym. He held posts at Halle (1866, 1867–1870) and Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer was a sinologist and tibetologist who studied at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Wilhelm Grube. He held posts at Columbia University (1905–1907) and the Field Museum of Natural History (1907).

Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a doctorate at the University of Munich and studied under Swami Lakshman Joo. She held posts at the Alice Boner Institute, the University of Vienna (1997), and the Abhinavagupta Research Library.

Bettine Birge is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University, studying under Wm. Theodore de Bary and Masaaki Sugiyama, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Paul Deussen, Emil Sieg, and Georg Simmel across several German universities. She taught at the University of Halle, University of London (~1934–1945), and University of Colombo (1945–1949).
